newsitem.title: JORDAN: U.S. delivers $100 mln military package to Jordan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. delivers $100 mln military package to Jordan.

text.p: The United States delivered battle tanks, helicopters and navy vessels worth $100 million to Jordan on Saturday, saying the kingdom had a pivotal role to play in Middle East peace.
U.S. ambassador to Jordan, Wesley Egan, said the equipment would bolster Jordan's fighting capabilities to confront what he said were continuing threats to stability in the region.

"The United States looks to Jordan as one of the most important, constructive, and moderate forces for peace," Egan told a news conference on the deck of the transport ship USS Cape Wrath, docked at Jordan's Red Sea port of Aqaba.

"This is still a region in which there are real threats... the ability of the Jordanian armed foces to meet those threats...is the fundamental rationale for the provision of this military equipment," Egan said.

The materiel is part of a military modernisation package worth over $300 million offered to Jordan in January in recognition of its new role in the Middle East after signing a 1994 peace treaty with Israel, ending a 46-year state of war.

King Hussein, once a close ally of Iraq's President Saddam Hussein, last year also turned against his former ally and called for change in Baghdad, completing Jordan's 100 degree realignment in the Middle East.
King Hussein has lobbied hard, with Israeli support, for U.S. help to revive his cash-strapped and increasingly dated armed forces.
The showpiece of the wider overall package is a squadron of 16 F-16 fighter bombers, due to be delivered at the end of next year.
The estimated $220 million cost of the jet squadron will be granted to Jordan over the four years until 1999, U.S. officials say.
"This is a fair and true indication of the fact that we are friends, that we stand together," a beaming King Hussein told the U.S. ambassador.
"The armed forces of Jordan...have been and will continue to be committed to the causes of stability, peace and security in this entire region."
Saturday's delivery includes 50 M60 A3 tanks, 18 UH-1H "Huey" helicopters, 250 trucks, a naval rescue boat, 2 light navy vessels, machine guns and 1,000 night vision goggles.
A giant C-130 transport plane will be delivered separately.
The equipment is used, but ready for immediate service.
"The helicopters fly, the tanks drive and shoot, and the utility vehicles are all fully operational," Egan said.
They were delivered under a drawdown programme of U.S. military stocks, approved by President Bill Clinton last February.

The size of the aid package is still modest compared to the hundreds of millions of dollars in military assistance pumped by Washington to Israel and Egypt every year since the two countries signed a peace treaty in 1979.

U.S. officials say military aid to Jordan this year also included around $25 million worth of equipment supplied under a regular Excess Defence Articles (EDA) programme, including 500 small trucks, rifles and medical supplies.
Clinton last month named Jordan a major non-Nato U.S. ally, entitling the kingdom for priority consideration for EDA assistance.
